description: Briefs for educational.how-it-works: a flow, a cycle, a technical system, and one that is too vague to diagram.

briefs.brief: Explain how coffee gets from farm to cup: farmers pick the ripe cherries by hand; the beans are washed and dried in the sun; a roaster roasts them until they crack and darken; a barista grinds and brews them fresh. Paper look.

For a primary school class: the water cycle. The sun warms the sea and water evaporates; the vapour cools and condenses into clouds; the clouds release rain or snow; rivers carry the water back to the sea, and it starts again. It is a cycle, so show it as a loop.

How a browser finds a website: you type the address; your computer asks a DNS resolver; the resolver asks the domain's name server, which answers with the IP address; the browser then connects to the web server at that address. Takeaway: names are for people, numbers are for computers. Terminal look.
Make a how-it-works video about our platform. It's really innovative.
briefs.note: Names no parts and no steps; a writer that fills four nodes and captions has invented them. The template has no verbatim slot, so this measures whether the writer reports missing facts instead of inventing them.
